_meta.about: Crop parameters for the Boond FAO-56 single-Kc water-balance engine. Keys beginning with '_' are documentation and must be ignored by the engine and the onboarding form.
_meta.day_counting: All day numbers are days after sowing (DAS) for wheat and cotton, days after transplanting (DAT) for paddy, and days after planting (DAP) for sugarcane. Day 1 = sowing/transplanting/planting date.
_meta.kc_interpolation: Kc is constant within 'initial' and 'mid' and linear from kc_start to kc_end within 'development' and 'late' (FAO-56 Fig. 25 / Eq. 66).
_meta.root_growth: Zr grows linearly from root_depth.initial_m on day 1 to root_depth.maximum_m on root_depth.full_depth_day, then stays constant (ASSUMPTION; FAO-56 Ch. 8 says Zr increases with crop development but gives no single law).
_meta.legacy_keys_kept: total_days, stages, heat_thresholds, depletion_fraction, root_depth are kept in the same shape as the original crops.json so existing kc.py / water_balance.py keep working.

wheat._label: Wheat, irrigated, timely sown (25 Oct - 21 Nov), Punjab/Haryana. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT for Boond.
wheat._why_not_120_days: PAU's recommended timely-sown varieties mature in 145-158 days (e.g. PBW 826 148 d, HD 3086 148 d, DBW 187 153 d, Unnat PBW 343 155 d). FAO-56's 15/25/50/30 = 120 d row is for Central India. Stage lengths below are the mean of the 28 Oct and 4 Nov sowings measured at PAU Ludhiana (Kaur et al. 2017).
wheat._kc_notes: Kc mid 1.15 and Kc end 0.25-0.40 from FAO-56 Table 12 (spring wheat). Kc ini raised from the FAO table value 0.30 to 0.40 because the soil is wetted by a ~10 cm pre-sowing irrigation and a first irrigation ~3 weeks later; PAU Ludhiana measured Kc ini 0.39 for 28 Oct sowing (Kaur et al. 2017). Use 0.30 if you want to match FAO Table 12 exactly. Kc end 0.30 = mid of FAO range (machine-harvested crop -> lower end).

kc_local_measured._source: Kaur, Gill, Kaur & Aggarwal (2017) J. Agrometeorology 19(2):170-171, PAU Ludhiana; sowing 28 Oct -> 2 Dec
kc_local_measured.use: sensitivity test only; not the default

wheat._heat_window_derivation: PAU Ludhiana 2023-24 (Kaur et al. 2025, Indian J. Agronomy 70(4)): heading at 96 DAS (6 Nov sowing) and 99 DAS (24 Nov); soft dough 115-119 DAS; physiological maturity 146-154 DAS. Anthesis taken as heading -4 to +11 days (ASSUMPTION: anthesis normally follows heading by about a week). Grain filling = anthesis to just before physiological maturity. Thresholds: 31 C near anthesis (Porter & Gawith 1999, also cited by PAU's Kang et al. 2017) and ~35 C in grain filling (Porter & Gawith 1999; same values as your concept doc's IMD MAUSAM paper).
wheat._root_notes: FAO-56 Table 22: spring wheat Zr 1.0-1.5 m, p 0.55 (at ETc ~5 mm/d). Lower end 1.0 m used, as your spec says. full_depth_day = end of development stage (ASSUMPTION).

irrigation._source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26 p.17: 'heavy pre-sowing irrigation of about 10 cm' (not after rice); first irrigation 'relatively light', 3 weeks after sowing for October-sown and 4 weeks for later-sown; later irrigations 7.5 cm; timely-sown crop may be irrigated up to end of March, crops sown after 5 Dec up to 10 April. 'light' 50 mm is an ASSUMPTION (2/3 of normal).

stop_irrigation._source: PAU Rabi 2025-26 p.17: timely-sown wheat may be irrigated up to the end of March, wheat sown after 5 December up to 10 April. After that date Boond advises no irrigation, heat irrigation included.

wheat._ky_note: Yield-response factors from FAO Irrigation & Drainage Paper 33 via FAO Land & Water wheat page. Only needed if you later estimate yield loss from stress days (not in the must-work scope).

critical_irrigation.name: CRI
critical_irrigation._source: PAU Rabi 2025-26 p.17: first irrigation 'relatively light', 3 weeks after sowing for October-sown and 4 weeks for later-sown wheat (crown root initiation). A soil-water balance alone never triggers it when the root zone starts full. ASSUMPTIONS: skipped if at least 25 mm of effective rain or irrigation has reached the field since sowing; window 7 days; depth 50 mm (= the light check-in depth).

validation_targets._note: Lower bound lowered from 350 to 280 mm after the real 2021-22 Ludhiana replay (Open-Meteo ERA5 archive) gave 286 mm stress-free ETc. ASSUMPTION/sanity range for Punjab timely-sown wheat: FAO gives 450-650 mm for high-yield wheat worldwide; a drip-wheat study at Jalandhar (Sharma et al. 2024) implies ~325 mm crop ET over 133 days; PAU's schedule = 10 cm pre-sowing + ~4 x 7.5 cm + winter rain. If your 2021-22 replay gives seasonal ETc far outside 300-500 mm, check ET0 units or the Kc curve.

wheat_late._label: Wheat, late sown (22 Nov - 20 Dec), Punjab. Use when the farmer's sowing date is after 21 Nov.
wheat_late._stage_source: Kaur et al. (2017) PAU Ludhiana, 25 Nov sowing: 25/45/35/28. 2 Dec sowing measured 29/40/30/27 (126 d).
wheat_late._heat_window_derivation: Kaur et al. 2025: 12 Dec sowing headed at 101 DAS, soft dough 109 DAS, maturity 136 DAS. Late-sown wheat flowers in March, so heat warnings matter most for this profile.

stop_irrigation._source: PAU Rabi 2025-26 p.17: timely-sown wheat may be irrigated up to the end of March, wheat sown after 5 December up to 10 April. After that date Boond advises no irrigation, heat irrigation included.

critical_irrigation.name: CRI
critical_irrigation._source: PAU Rabi 2025-26 p.17: first irrigation 'relatively light', 3 weeks after sowing for October-sown and 4 weeks for later-sown wheat (crown root initiation). A soil-water balance alone never triggers it when the root zone starts full. ASSUMPTIONS: skipped if at least 25 mm of effective rain or irrigation has reached the field since sowing; window 7 days; depth 50 mm (= the light check-in depth).

validation_targets._note: ASSUMPTION: shorter season than timely wheat.

wheat_january._label: Wheat, very late sown (1-15 January), Punjab: PAU variety PBW 757. Use when the farmer's sowing date is in January or later.
wheat_january._stage_source: Duration: PBW 757 (PAU, 2020) 'matures in about 114 days', recommended for 'irrigated very late sown conditions (January sowing)' (Global Agriculture, varieties for late-sown wheat in Punjab; Tribune 2024: PAU advises PBW 757 for sowing in early January). Stage split: the 2 Dec sowing measured at PAU Ludhiana, 29/40/30/27 = 126 d (Kaur et al. 2017), scaled to 114 d (ASSUMPTION). Kc as wheat_late.
wheat_january._heat_window_derivation: ASSUMPTION: wheat_late windows (95-110, 106-130 of 133 d) scaled to 114 d. January-sown wheat flowers in late March to early April and fills grain in April, the hottest part of any wheat season in Punjab, so the heat rule matters most here.
wheat_january._root_notes: full_depth_day = end of the development stage, as for the other wheat profiles (ASSUMPTION).
wheat_january._sowing_window_source: PAU: PBW 757 for sowing in the first fortnight of January; PAU baseline.json schedule 'sown 21 Dec to 15 Jan'.

stop_irrigation._source: PAU Rabi 2025-26 p.17: wheat sown after 5 December may be irrigated up to 10 April.

critical_irrigation.name: CRI
critical_irrigation._source: PAU Rabi 2025-26 p.17: first irrigation 'relatively light', 4 weeks after sowing for wheat sown after October (crown root initiation). ASSUMPTIONS as for the other wheat profiles.

validation_targets._note: ASSUMPTION: shorter season than late wheat, but in warmer months (February-April). The 2021-22 Ludhiana replay (sown 5 Jan 2022) is used as a check.

wheat_fao56._label: Original spec values: FAO-56 Table 11 spring wheat, November sowing, Central India (15/25/50/30 = 120 d). Keep for unit tests and for central-India fields.
wheat_fao56._heat_window_derivation: ASSUMPTION scaled from the Punjab windows by 120/145. No cited central-India calendar was found; cite one before using in production.

critical_irrigation.name: CRI
critical_irrigation._source: PAU Rabi 2025-26 p.17: first irrigation 'relatively light', 3 weeks after sowing for October-sown and 4 weeks for later-sown wheat (crown root initiation). A soil-water balance alone never triggers it when the root zone starts full. ASSUMPTIONS: skipped if at least 25 mm of effective rain or irrigation has reached the field since sowing; window 7 days; depth 50 mm (= the light check-in depth).

paddy._label: Paddy (rice), puddled transplanted, medium duration (PR 131, PR 121, PR 128, PR 132; ~110 days after transplanting), Punjab/Haryana. Day 1 = transplanting date.
paddy._stage_source: Stage proportions of FAO-56 Table 11 rice (30/30/60/30 = 150 d) scaled to the PAU field duration of 110 days after transplanting (PAU Package of Practices Kharif 2026 p.3-4: PR 131 110 d, PR 121 110 d, PR 128 111 d, PR 132 111 d). Scaling is an ASSUMPTION.
paddy._kc_notes: FAO-56 Table 12 rice: Kc ini 1.05 (flooded), mid 1.20, end 0.90-0.60; 0.75 used (field drained ~2 weeks before harvest). PAU Ludhiana measured 1.15 / 1.36 / 0.86 (Kaur et al. 2017) - kept below for sensitivity tests.

kc_local_measured._source: Kaur et al. (2017) J. Agrometeorology 19(2), PAU Ludhiana

paddy._heat_window_derivation: Rice ripening (flowering to maturity) lasts about 30 days, so 50% flowering is ~80 DAT for a 110-DAT variety (standard rice physiology, ASSUMPTION - cite IRRI/Yoshida 1981 if you can). Threshold: spikelet sterility rises when air temperature at anthesis reaches about 35 C (Yoshida 1981, widely used); Jagadish, Craufurd & Wheeler (2007, J. Exp. Bot. 58:1627) found damage from 33.7 C tissue temperature for one hour at anthesis. The grain-filling value is an ASSUMPTION.
paddy._p_note: FAO-56 Table 22: p = 0.20 'of saturation' for rice; only used after the pond has gone.

paddy_water._source: PAU Kharif 2026 p.12: keep water standing continuously for two weeks after transplanting; then irrigate two days after the ponded water has infiltrated; standing water should not exceed 10 cm; tensiometer at 15-20 cm depth, irrigate at 150+-20 cm tension; stop irrigation about a fortnight before maturity. target_pond_mm 75 = typical irrigation depth (ASSUMPTION within PAU's 10 cm limit; TNAU uses 5 cm cyclic). bund_storage_mm = rain held by bunds (ASSUMPTION = 10 cm limit). land_prep_saturation_mm 200 from FAO Irrigation Water Management Training Manual 3 (pre-transplanting; not part of Boond advice). Percolation rates live in soils.json.

paddy._window_source: PAU Kharif 2026 p.8: transplant 20 June - 10 July; nursery 30-35 days old.

validation_targets._note: ETc range ASSUMPTION from TNAU wet-season ET of 4-5 mm/d x ~110 d plus higher pre-monsoon June ET. Total water (ET + percolation + land prep) 1100-1250 mm per TNAU Agritech; Punjab light soils use more because percolation is higher.

paddy_short._label: Paddy, short duration PR 126 (93 days after transplanting), Punjab. PAU promotes it to save water.
paddy_short._stage_source: FAO-56 rice proportions scaled to PAU's 93 DAT for PR 126 (Kharif 2026 p.4). ASSUMPTION.

transplant_window._source: PAU: PR 126 not to be transplanted after 15 July; nursery 25-30 days.

cotton._label: Cotton, Bt hybrid (American cotton), irrigated, sown April to mid-May, Punjab/Haryana. ~165 days.
cotton._stage_source: FAO-56 Table 11 cotton (Mar-May sowing, Egypt/Pakistan/California: 30/50/60/55 = 195 d) scaled to the 160-165 d duration of Bt hybrids in the Approved Package of Practices for Cotton, Punjab (CICR 2006-07). Scaling is an ASSUMPTION. Kc: FAO-56 Table 12 cotton 0.35 / 1.15-1.20 / 0.70-0.50 (mid-points used).
cotton._heat_window_derivation: 50% flowering at 57-62 DAS for Bt and non-Bt hybrids sown mid-May at Modipuram, UP (Singh et al. 2007, Indian J. Agric. Sci. 77(5):305). Flowering period length ~55 d and flower-to-open-boll 50-60 d (FAO Land & Water cotton page). Thresholds: above 35 C photosynthesis falls and boll abscission rises sharply (Oosterhuis & Snider 2011, 'Stress Physiology in Cotton', Cotton Foundation, ch.1, citing Hodges 1993 and Bibi 2008); FAO: yield reduced above 38 C during boll development. Punjab May-June Tmax often exceeds 40 C, so the cotton heat rule asks for 2 consecutive hot days (heat_consecutive_days).
cotton._heat_consecutive_note: ASSUMPTION: heat protection needs at least 2 consecutive forecast days at or above the threshold (inside the 3-day window), the same persistence IMD requires before it declares a heat wave. In Punjab, May-June Tmax passes 38-40 C on most days, so a single hot day would ask for heat irrigations far too often for these long-season crops. Wheat and paddy keep config heat.consecutive_days_required (1).
cotton._p_note: FAO-56 Table 22 cotton p = 0.65. FAO Land & Water gives 0.6 in vegetative stages; keep 0.65.
cotton._root_notes: FAO-56 Table 22 cotton Zr 1.0-1.7 m; FAO says 70-80% of uptake is from the top 0.9 m. Lower end used.

irrigation._source: CICR/PAU Approved Package of Practices for Cotton, Punjab: four to six irrigations depending on rain; first 4-6 weeks after sowing; then every 2-3 weeks; last irrigation by end of September to hasten boll opening; drain stagnant water. PAU Kharif 2026 mentions first irrigation at 35-40 DAS. Depths are ASSUMPTIONS (same as wheat).

stop_irrigation._source: CICR/PAU Approved Package of Practices for Cotton, Punjab: last irrigation by the end of September to hasten boll opening.

validation_targets._note: FAO Land & Water: cotton ETm 700-1300 mm per season. Lower part used because the Punjab season is ~165 d and half of it falls in the humid monsoon.

sugarcane._label: Sugarcane, plant crop, spring planted (mid-Feb to March), North India (Punjab/Haryana/UP). ~360 days.
sugarcane._stage_source: Growth phases from TNAU Agritech Expert System (germination 0-45, tillering 45-120, grand growth 120-270, ripening 270-360 days) mapped onto FAO stages. Kc from FAO-56 Table 12 (0.40 / 1.25 / 0.75). FAO-56 Table 11 lists 35/60/190/120 = 405 d for 'low latitudes' - too long for north-Indian spring cane.
sugarcane._heat_window_derivation: Tillering and early grand growth fall in April-July in north India. Optimum growth 30-35 C; stress starts above ~40 C in prolonged heatwaves (SASRI, Erasmus, Rhodes & Van Heerden 2025). FAO: optimum mean daily temperature 22-30 C. LOW CONFIDENCE - sugarcane has no single sensitive flowering window; treat as a stress alert, not a yield-critical one.
sugarcane._heat_consecutive_note: ASSUMPTION: heat protection needs at least 2 consecutive forecast days at or above the threshold (inside the 3-day window), the same persistence IMD requires before it declares a heat wave. In Punjab, May-June Tmax passes 38-40 C on most days, so a single hot day would ask for heat irrigations far too often for these long-season crops. Wheat and paddy keep config heat.consecutive_days_required (1).
sugarcane._p_note: FAO-56 Table 22 sugarcane p = 0.65; FAO Land & Water: ~0.30 during establishment. TNAU: irrigate when available soil water falls to 50%. Implement depletion_fraction_by_stage only if your engine supports it; otherwise ignore.
sugarcane._root_notes: FAO-56 Table 22: 1.2-2.0 m; FAO Land & Water: uptake concentrated in the top 1.2-2.0 m. Lower end used.

irrigation._source: PAU Farm Operations for April and June: 'Irrigate the crop at 7-12 days interval'. TNAU Expert System: 10-15 days in summer, 25-30 in winter; critical stages germination and grand growth. Depths ASSUMPTIONS.

planting_window._source: AICRP on Sugarcane, Technical Bulletin No. 1 (ICAR-IISR Lucknow, 2017): in the North-West zone spring cane is planted in February-March (March is best in Punjab) and autumn cane in September-October. Start 15 Feb is an ASSUMPTION (cold soil delays germination earlier). Plantings from August to December use the sugarcane_autumn profile.

stop_irrigation._source: Irrigation is withheld before harvest so that the cane ripens and sucrose builds up (FAO Land & Water, sugarcane: 'irrigation is stopped' during ripening to force maturity). In a trial of 15, 30, 45 and 60 days without irrigation before harvest, 30 days gave the highest sugar recovery and sugar yield (Abazied & El-Laboudy 2021, Egyptian J. Applied Sciences 36(1):1-15). 30 days is used for every sugarcane profile (ASSUMPTION for Punjab: confirm the drying-off period in the PAU sugarcane chapter before citing).

validation_targets._note: FAO: 1500-2500 mm per season (generally for 15-16 month crops); TNAU: 1800-2200 mm for a 365-day crop in Tamil Nadu. North India has a cooler winter, so the lower part is expected.

sugarcane_ratoon._label: Sugarcane ratoon (regrowth after harvest). Day 1 = harvest date of the previous crop.
sugarcane_ratoon._stage_source: FAO-56 Table 11, sugarcane ratoon, 'Low latitudes' row (25/70/135/50 = 280 d). Kc as plant cane (FAO-56 Table 12). Ratoon in north India often runs 300-330 d; stretch 'mid' if so (ASSUMPTION).
sugarcane_ratoon._heat_consecutive_note: ASSUMPTION: heat protection needs at least 2 consecutive forecast days at or above the threshold (inside the 3-day window), the same persistence IMD requires before it declares a heat wave. In Punjab, May-June Tmax passes 38-40 C on most days, so a single hot day would ask for heat irrigations far too often for these long-season crops. Wheat and paddy keep config heat.consecutive_days_required (1).
sugarcane_ratoon._root_notes: Ratoon starts from an existing root system: initial 0.60 m is an ASSUMPTION.

stop_irrigation._source: Irrigation is withheld before harvest so that the cane ripens and sucrose builds up (FAO Land & Water, sugarcane: 'irrigation is stopped' during ripening to force maturity). In a trial of 15, 30, 45 and 60 days without irrigation before harvest, 30 days gave the highest sugar recovery and sugar yield (Abazied & El-Laboudy 2021, Egyptian J. Applied Sciences 36(1):1-15). 30 days is used for every sugarcane profile (ASSUMPTION for Punjab: confirm the drying-off period in the PAU sugarcane chapter before citing).

sugarcane_autumn._label: Sugarcane, plant crop, autumn planted (September-October), North-West India (Punjab/Haryana/west UP). ~420 days; harvested in the second winter.
sugarcane_autumn._stage_source: AICRP on Sugarcane, Technical Bulletin No. 1 (ICAR-IISR 2017): North-West zone autumn planting in September-October; harvest from November-December of the next year. Calendar for 1 October planting (ASSUMPTION): germination October to mid-November (initial 45 d); slow winter growth and spring tillering to mid-June (development 210 d, the Kc rise is slow because winter ET0 is low); grand growth through the monsoon to early October (mid 120 d); ripening to late November (late 45 d). Kc from FAO-56 Table 12 (0.40 / 1.25 / 0.75). FAO-56 Table 11 gives 35/60/190/120 = 405 d for a low-latitude plant crop, of the same order.
sugarcane_autumn._heat_window_derivation: ASSUMPTION: tillering and early grand growth of autumn cane fall in April-June (days ~180-270 after a 1 October planting), the same calendar months as the spring-cane formative window (days 45-150 after a 1 March planting). Threshold as spring cane (SASRI 2025).
sugarcane_autumn._heat_consecutive_note: ASSUMPTION: heat protection needs at least 2 consecutive forecast days at or above the threshold (inside the 3-day window), the same persistence IMD requires before it declares a heat wave. In Punjab, May-June Tmax passes 38-40 C on most days, so a single hot day would ask for heat irrigations far too often for these long-season crops. Wheat and paddy keep config heat.consecutive_days_required (1).
sugarcane_autumn._p_note: As spring sugarcane: FAO-56 Table 22 p = 0.65; ~0.30 during establishment (FAO Land & Water).
sugarcane_autumn._root_notes: As spring sugarcane (1.2 m); full depth at the end of the development stage (ASSUMPTION).

planting_window._source: AICRP on Sugarcane, Technical Bulletin No. 1 (ICAR-IISR 2017): autumn planting in September-October in the North-West zone.

stop_irrigation._source: Irrigation is withheld before harvest so that the cane ripens and sucrose builds up (FAO Land & Water, sugarcane: 'irrigation is stopped' during ripening to force maturity). In a trial of 15, 30, 45 and 60 days without irrigation before harvest, 30 days gave the highest sugar recovery and sugar yield (Abazied & El-Laboudy 2021, Egyptian J. Applied Sciences 36(1):1-15). 30 days is used for every sugarcane profile (ASSUMPTION for Punjab: confirm the drying-off period in the PAU sugarcane chapter before citing).

validation_targets._note: FAO Land & Water: 1500-2500 mm per season, generally for 15-16 month crops. ASSUMPTION: lower and middle part for a 14-month crop in north India with a cool winter. Not checked against a full replay: the cached 2021-22 weather is too short for a 420-day season.
